title: microhandshake-prefetch-protocol-and-sdk-telemetry-scratch
content:
Purpose

Quick working draft that sketches a compact 'micro-handshake' + prefetch protocol for hosted streaming calls where the model can request tool invocations, emit typed/structured fragments, and clients can resume or apply backpressure with minimal RTT. This doc prioritizes practical SDK ergonomics and telemetry hooks for rollout testing.

Context / problem
- Current streaming surface mixes large frames for tool calls and free-form text which hurts incremental render and increases wasted tokens on mobile clients.
- Tool calling often requires multiple synchronous round-trips: model decides action -> server mediates -> client executes -> result round-trips. That adds latency and fragile retry semantics.
- Developers want: low-latency visible partial results, deterministic tool transactions, idempotent retries, and clear telemetry slices to evaluate fidelity regressions.

High-level goals
- Define a compact handshake that establishes a session capability vector (supports-prefetch, accept-partial-json, prefer-atomic-tool-tx).
- Allow speculative prefetch of tool results (client or server-side) to hide latency while preserving eventual correctness via transactional commit/fallback.
- Make SDK ergonomics simple: 3 primitives (openSession, onFrame, commitToolResult) with clear failure modes and opt-in telemetry events.
- Ensure structured fragments (JSONL-like) are first-class; make resumable sessions deterministic for replay and tests.

Non-goals
- Full rewrite of streaming wire protocol. This is a complementary lightweight layer on top of existing streaming frames.
- Handling arbitrary long-running tool jobs (out-of-band workflows are out of scope for this iteration).

User stories
- As a mobile app dev, I want partial structured fields to show in UI as soon as they arrive so users can act while heavy tool calls complete.
- As a platform engineer, I want telemetry hooks that let me measure tool-invocation latency distribution and speculative prefetch hit rates to tune cost/accuracy tradeoffs.
- As a backend engineer, I want deterministic idempotent tool commits so retries do not double-charge downstream systems.

Core protocol sketch
- Session open: client calls openSession(metadata) -> server replies with sessionId and capability_flags. Capability_flags example: ["PREFETCH_OK","PARTIAL_JSON","ATOMIC_TOOL_TX"]
- Micro-handshake: small two-way exchange allowing client to communicate that it can do local prefetch (e.g., cached DB, local index) or prefers server-side prefetch. This guides the runtime on how to schedule speculative fetches.
- Frames: define three compact frame types added to streaming channel: FRAG (partial structured fragment), TOOL_REQ (model asks for tool), TOOL_PRE (prefetch hint), TOOL_COMMIT (final tool output commit), and TOOL_ABORT. Frames are newline-delimited JSONL envelopes with an explicit sequence id.
- Example FRAG payload: {"seq":42,"type":"FRAG","schema":"search_result_v1","payload":"{...}"}

Speculative prefetch flow (happy path)
1) Model emits TOOL_REQ for external_search with args. It may attach a prefetch_hint (timeout budget, preferred fidelity).
2) Server consults session capability: if client.prefetch_local==true and a cached value exists, server sends TOOL_PRE with cached token and marks state speculative=true.
3) Client receives TOOL_PRE and renders optimistic UI. If the server later sends TOOL_COMMIT that differs, client reconciles using a small patch diff (server includes patch delta where possible).
4) If commit never arrives (timeout), client either rolls back optimistic UI or shows 'stale' indicator.

Transactional tool semantics
- Tools are executed as transactions identified by (sessionId, seq, toolName). Each commit includes a commit_id and signature to allow idempotent apply.
- Server maintains lightweight lease with expiry; retries use commit_id to dedupe.
- TOOL_COMMIT frames must include a minimal audit header: {"commit_id":"c123","applied_at":"2026-02-25T15:02:00Z","source":"server|client-cache","checksum":"sha256:..."}.

SDK ergonomics (JS + mobile notes)
- OpenSession(opts) -> returns session object with: session.id, capabilities, telemetry_token.
- session.on('frame', handler) -> handler receives typed frames: {kind:"FRAG"|"TOOL_REQ"|... , seq, payload}
- session.callTool(toolName, args, opts) -> returns a Promise that resolves with the canonical commit or rejects with clear recoverable/terminal error types.
- commitToolResult(seq, commitPayload) -> explicitly used by SDKs that run tool locally and then notify the runtime; runtime then broadcasts TOOL_COMMIT.
- Backpressure: SDK exposes session.pause() / session.resume() which instructs server to slow speculative prefetch and reduce batch sizes. Server should respect pause within 50–200ms window.

Telemetry hooks and observability
- Emit events: session.open, frame.received (with kind), tool.prefetch_hit, tool.commit_latency_ms, speculative-reconcile-rate, frame-drop.
- Tagging: telemetry_token ties events to route/model/version and customer_id (if present); avoid PII in events.
- Dashboards to build: prefetch-hit-rate over time, reconcile rate (how often TOOL_COMMIT differs from TOOL_PRE), average first-fragment-latency, tail latencies for TOOL_COMMIT.

Structured output and schema negotiation
- FRAG frames include schema urls and version tags. Offer a small schema registry approach: client can request 'shape-only' metadata to render placeholders quickly.
- Backwards compatibility: allow schema version fallback (client declares accepted_versions array during openSession). Server may send legacy-frag entries if necessary.

Degradation and failover modes
- If commit never materializes: show stale badge or attempt re-run of tool on client (opt-in).
- If tool system overloaded: server can send TOOL_ABORT with reason and suggested fallback (e.g., lower_fidelity:true).

Security and audit considerations
- Tool commits must be auditable: commit_id, source, checksum. Keep an append-only audit log per session in the control plane for enterprise customers (subject to retention policy).
- Clients must be able to opt-out of speculative prefetch for sensitive data via capability flag during openSession.

Migration and rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> GA)
- MVP (Q1): implement FRAG + TOOL_REQ + TOOL_COMMIT frames, basic SDK wiring, telemetry events (session.open, frame.received, commit_latency). Beta (Q2): prefetch hints + speculative rendering + reconcile metrics. GA (Q3): transactional idempotency guarantees, audit logs, enterprise toggles.

APIs + thin client examples
- JS (browser):
  const s = openSession({model:'x-large', acceptPartialJson:true});
  s.on('frame', f => { if(f.kind=='FRAG') renderFragment(f.payload); });
  const res = await s.callTool('web_search', {q:'latest quarterly results'}, {speculative:true});

Open questions
- How big should prefetch budgets be by default? (10–200ms?) We should A/B test tradeoffs between cost and reconcile rate.
- Patch format for reconciles: line-based diff vs field-level patch. Field-level is cleaner for structured output but increases spec complexity.
- Exact telemetry token format and PII minimization strategy.

Next steps / action items
- Engineering: spike a server prototype that can emit TOOL_PRE and reconcile with TOOL_COMMIT within an existing streaming session (ENG-2148).
- SDK: design minimal surface for commitToolResult and backpressure APIs (Marcus).
- Product: define default prefetch budget per-tier and flag gating for enterprise (Sofia).

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a lightweight layer — goal is to enable common engineering patterns (optimistic UI, deterministic commits) without forcing an entirely new wire protocol. Look for simplicity in SDK surface and clear telemetry signals.
